titleText.es: Curiosidad: En realidad Elain es su segundo nombre.
titleText.en: Trivia: Elaine is actually her middle name.
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish archive title text visibly spells the name Elain, without the final e.

regions.labelEs: ENTONCES, ¿EL MEJOR HACKER DE NUESTRA ERA ES UNA MAMÁ DE LAS DE COCINAR GALLETAS?

applications.explanationEn: The first de places the mother in an understood feminine group, las stands for its members, and the second de introduces cocinar galletas as their characteristic action.

applications.exampleEs: A SU HIJO BOBBY NUNCA LE FUERON LOS ORDENADORES
applications.explanationEn: A su hijo names the person whose taste is described, nunca makes the preference negative, le repeats that experiencer before the verb, and plural fueron agrees with los ordenadores.
Elaine is the stated subject, so tenía refers to what she possessed in this occurrence.
Tenía supplies the past form of tener, un don names the natural ability, and para ellos identifies the field to which that ability applies.

cards.noteEn: With el, la, lo, los, or las, mejor usually means “best.” Without one of those words, it often means “better.”

cards.answerEn: of; among (introducing a type or group)
cards.noteEn: In de los de or de las de, this first de places someone among a recognizable type of people.

example.es: Pablo es de los de llegar pronto.
example.en: Pablo is one of those people who arrive early.

cards.promptEs: de los/las de + verbo en forma de diccionario
cards.questionEn: How can you describe someone as one of the kind of people who characteristically do a certain action?
cards.answerEn: Use de los de for a masculine group or de las de for a feminine group, then give the action verb in its unchanged dictionary form.
cards.noteEn: The first de places the person in a group. Los or las matches that understood group, and the second de introduces the typical action. The action verb stays in its dictionary form—the unchanged form ending in -ar, -er, or -ir.

example.es: Lucía es de las de llegar temprano.
example.en: Lucía is one of those people who arrive early.

cards.noteEn: Las can stand without a repeated feminine plural noun when the missing group is already understood.

cards.answerEn: who; the kind that (introducing a typical action)
cards.noteEn: The second de in de los de or de las de introduces the action that characterizes that type of person.

example.es: Soy de los de caminar al trabajo.
example.en: I am one of those people who walk to work.

cards.noteEn: Eh can show that the speaker is surprised or did not understand what was just said.
Tuvo is a completed-past form of tener, “to have.” The subject supplied by context tells whether it means she or he.
Hijos can mean sons, but the masculine plural also commonly refers to a group of children that includes a daughter.

example.es: Tienen un hijo y una hija: dos hijos en total.
example.en: They have a son and a daughter: two children in total.

cards.answerEn: to; for (introducing whose tastes are described)
cards.noteEn: With the informal preference use of ir, a can introduce the person whose tastes are described; a short word such as le normally repeats that person before the verb.

example.es: A Daniel le van los deportes.

cards.promptEs: irle algo a alguien, con sentido de gustos
cards.questionEn: How do you say that something suits someone or is their kind of thing?
cards.answerEn: Put me, te, le, nos, os, or les before a form of ir that matches the thing that suits or appeals.
cards.noteEn: The short word identifies the person whose taste is described. The form of ir matches the thing that appeals, not that person: va for one thing and van for several things in the present; another time frame can use forms such as fue or fueron. Os identifies more than one person addressed informally in Spain. This preference use is especially common in informal Spanish in Spain.

example.en: Quiet films are my kind of thing.

cards.answerEn: marks the person whose preference or reaction is described
cards.noteEn: With gustar and similar preference expressions, le identifies the person experiencing the liking, appeal, or reaction. The thing that causes that reaction controls whether the verb is singular or plural, while le stays the same.

example.es: A Luis le gustan los trenes.

cards.answerEn: they suited him; they were his kind of thing
cards.noteEn: Fueron is the completed-past plural form of ir. With me, te, le, nos, or les, ir can say that plural things suit or appeal to someone rather than that they physically go somewhere.

example.es: Nunca me fueron las fiestas grandes.
example.en: Big parties were never my thing.

cards.noteEn: Tenía is a past form of tener. It presents a state or characteristic that held at that past time without marking its beginning or end.

cards.promptEs: tener un don para + actividad o tema
cards.questionEn: How do you say that someone has a natural gift for an activity or subject?
cards.answerEn: Use a form of tener, then un don para, then name the activity or subject.
cards.noteEn: Tener changes for the person and time. Un don remains the noun for a natural gift, and para introduces the field in which that ability appears. The plus sign in the prompt means “followed by.”

example.es: Clara tiene un don para los idiomas.
example.en: Clara has a gift for languages.

cards.answerEn: for; with (introducing what a talent applies to)
cards.noteEn: After don or talento, para introduces the subject, activity, or field in which the person is gifted.

example.en: She has a talent for music.

cards.answerEn: them (masculine or mixed group, after a preposition)
cards.noteEn: Ellos usually means ‘they,’ but after a preposition such as con, para, or sin, English uses ‘them.’
Cumplió is a completed-past form of cumplir. Before a number of años, it states the age someone reached.

cards.questionEn: How do you say that someone turns a particular age?
cards.answerEn: Use a form of cumplir, then the age number, then años.
cards.noteEn: Cumplir changes for the person and time; the number states the age reached. Spanish literally treats the birthday as completing that many years. Each plus sign in the prompt means “followed by.”
Años is the plural of año. Keep the ñ: anos without it is a different word.

example.en: We lived there for two years.

cards.promptEs: enviar a alguien a + verbo en forma de diccionario
cards.questionEn: How do you say that someone sends another person to do an action?
cards.answerEn: Use a form of enviar, identify the person sent, add a, and keep the action verb in its unchanged dictionary form.
cards.noteEn: Enviar changes for the sender and time. The person sent can be named or represented by a short word such as lo or la. The following a links that person to the assigned action, whose verb stays in its dictionary form ending in -ar, -er, or -ir.

example.es: El jefe envió a Marta a buscar ayuda.
example.en: The boss sent Marta to look for help.

cards.noteEn: Envió is a completed-past form of enviar, “to send.” The written accent distinguishes it from envío, which can mean “I send” or “shipment.”

cards.answerEn: to (linking a verb to the following infinitive)
an influential computer scientist and author of The Art of Computer Programming
cards.noteEn: Knuth taught at Stanford and is a natural authority to cite about algorithms and programming conventions.
Estudió is a completed-past form of estudiar. The written accent marks the stressed final syllable.
Write the question form as two words, with an accent on qué. Write the usual answer word porque as one word without an accent.
cards.questionEn: How do you write “why” and “because” in Spanish?

example.es: ¿Por qué estudias español? Porque me gusta.
example.en: Why do you study Spanish? Because I like it.

cards.answerEn: a pathfinding algorithm that combines the cost already traveled with an estimate of the cost still remaining
cards.noteEn: A* usually keeps many possible routes in memory while choosing which one looks most promising. That memory demand is the issue tested in the training scene.
Here uso names the act or amount of using something. The same spelling can also be a verb meaning “I use,” so the surrounding words determine which meaning applies.

example.es: El uso del teléfono está prohibido.

cards.noteEn: Here memoria refers to computer storage used while an algorithm runs, not a person's ability to remember.

example.en: The program uses a lot of memory.

cards.noteEn: Usarías keeps the whole dictionary form usar and adds -ías for one familiar “you.” It presents the choice as hypothetical.

cards.questionEn: How do you form a Spanish “would” verb such as “would forget”?
cards.answerEn: Keep the whole dictionary form and add a conditional ending such as -ía.
cards.noteEn: The same endings attach to verbs ending in -ar, -er, and -ir. The ending changes for the person: -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -íais, or -ían.

cards.questionEn: Why might Spanish say tú or yo when the verb already tells you who acts?
cards.answerEn: Say the subject pronoun to add emphasis, contrast, or clarity; otherwise Spanish often leaves it out.
cards.noteEn: A verb form such as eres already points to “you.” Adding tú can stress that particular person, especially in a contrast or a surprised question. The pronoun may appear after the verb.

cards.answerEn: an algorithm for finding shortest paths through a graph whose edge costs are nonnegative
cards.noteEn: It repeatedly expands the not-yet-finished point with the lowest known total cost. Unlike A*, it does not use an estimate of the remaining distance; the contrast supplies the technical content of the answer in the scene.
De can join an invention, theorem, or named object to the person whose name it bears. English may instead use an adjective based on that name.

cards.promptEs: hasta que + hecho habitual o conocido
cards.questionEn: What verb form follows hasta que for a usual or already-known event?
cards.answerEn: Use an ordinary statement form when the event is habitual, known, or already completed.
cards.noteEn: Hasta que means “until.” Spanish uses an ordinary statement form for an event treated as a fact. A still-awaited future event instead uses the special subjunctive form; for example, llega is an ordinary form, while llegue is the corresponding subjunctive form.

example.es: Siempre leo hasta que empieza la clase.
example.en: I always read until class starts.

cards.noteEn: Superó is a completed-past form of superar. It says that someone exceeded another person's level or performance.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; marks a specific person as the object
cards.noteEn: Spanish generally places a before a specific person who receives a verb’s action. This “personal a” is not translated as a separate English word.

cards.promptEs: a + persona o expresión que se refiere a una persona
cards.questionEn: Why does Spanish sometimes put a before the person affected by an action?
cards.answerEn: Put a before a person—or a word such as alguien or nadie—when that person directly receives the action.
cards.noteEn: This a is called the personal a. It is common before a named or specific person, but person-denoting words such as alguien (“someone”) and nadie (“nobody”) also take it. English usually has no separate word for it. Before the masculine article el, a + el contracts to al.
In mathematics and computer science, a cota is a value or growth rate that a quantity cannot pass in a specified direction.

example.es: Buscamos una cota para el error.
example.en: We are looking for a bound on the error.

cards.questionEn: What Spanish term means a mathematical or computational lower bound?
cards.answerEn: Use cota inferior for a proven minimum that a quantity or resource requirement cannot beat.
cards.noteEn: Cota names a bound, and inferior specifies the lower direction. In algorithm analysis, a lower bound can state that every solution must take at least a certain amount of time or work; the exact mathematical rate is supplied separately.

example.es: El problema tiene una cota inferior conocida.
example.en: The problem has a known lower bound.

cards.noteEn: After cota, inferior identifies a minimum boundary rather than simply describing something as lower in physical position.

cards.questionEn: How do you say that a calculation or attempt gives someone a particular result?
cards.answerEn: Put me, te, le, nos, os, or les before a form of salir, then state the result obtained.
cards.noteEn: The short word identifies who gets the result. Salir changes for the result and time; sale is the present singular form. This is not the ordinary movement meaning “to leave.” The plus sign in the prompt means “followed by.”
Salir normally means “to leave” or “to go out,” but with a calculation or attempt it can describe the result that comes out.

Le usually marks an indirect object, such as a recipient (“to him”). With a masculine person, especially in Spain, le can also be used as the direct object (“him”); this accepted use is called leísmo.

example.es: Le di el libro a Pablo.

cards.noteEn: Abandonó is a completed-past form of abandonar. The subject supplied by context tells who performed the action.
